brief.headline: Memory makers ride hyperscaler capex surge; SK Hynix extends HBM lead as Samsung chases qualification
brief.summary: <cite index="41-8">Samsung Electronics traded at 272,500 won, up 5.21%, while SK hynix traded at 1,959,000 won, up 6.70%</cite> as of July 22 morning in Seoul. <cite index="8-3,8-13">Top three memory makers have allocated full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding for 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="15-1,15-2">DRAM contract prices projected to rise 13-18% in Q3, NAND Flash 10-15% QoQ, aligning with TrendForce forecasts</cite>. <cite index="27-1">Hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending reaches $725B in 2026, up 77% from $410B in 2025</cite>. <cite index="29-4,29-6">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from 20% currently to 10% by end-2026, with monthly capacity reaching 120,000-140,000 wafers</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%</cite>. <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix expected to maintain ~50% HBM market share in 2026</cite>. <cite index="43-2,43-3">SK hynix ADRs closed up 13.75% overnight; top 1% traders at Mirae Asset net-bought Samsung Electronics while net-selling SK hynix on July 22</cite>, suggesting tactical profit-taking on momentum. Samsung qualification risk on HBM3E for Nvidia remains overhang vs. Hynix's <cite index="8-9">exclusive ability to deliver both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale</cite>. Relative: long SK Hynix vs. Samsung on structural HBM share and earlier HBM4 ramp, but watch Samsung's <cite index="41-10">next-gen HBM4 memory unveiling</cite> as potential catalyst to close gap.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-10">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026</cite>, decelerating to <cite index="15-2">13-18% projected increase in Q3</cite>. <cite index="8-11">Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026, NAND +45%, with ASPs climbing >30%</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected to last through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historical cycles</cite>. <cite index="8-5">Capacity pre-sold due to HBM prioritization, tightening mainstream DRAM/NAND for consumer/industrial electronics</cite>. Watch for demand elasticity as <cite index="16-4,16-5">higher memory costs feed into retail pricing, potentially weighing on PC shipments and smartphone production plans</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits; UBS points to TSMC's latest call as evidence AI demand running well ahead of forecasts</cite>. <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only minimal to modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs. 2025</cite> despite <cite index="5-4">Nvidia negotiations with suppliers and possible pricing pushback as Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification</cite>. <cite index="8-2">HBM3E expected to remain dominant AI memory through the year, with pricing power intact until new capacity comes online after 2027</cite>. <cite index="42-1">Samsung and SK Hynix signed letter of intent with OpenAI in October 2025 for eventual supply of 900,000 DRAM wafers/month for Stargate project</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Micron announced integration of HBM3E 36GB 12-high offering into AMD Instinct MI350 Series</cite>; <cite index="46-2">HBM4 chips expected to be main AI memory for Nvidia's next-gen Rubin architecture</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix surge on U.S. semiconductor rally; Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +5.21%
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="41-1,41-6">Nextrade up 4%+ on open; buying flowed into major domestic semiconductor stocks as chip shares rallied across board on NYSE overnight and AI investment expectations revived</cite>. Momentum trade extends memory multiples.

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns Q3 2026 DRAM prices +20-30%, NAND +35-40% as memory crunch persists
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="11-8">ADATA Chairman stated memory manufacturers announced DRAM contract prices will continue to rise 20-30% in Q3, NAND Flash prices also increasing</cite>. <cite index="11-11">Shortages expected to last till 2028 if AI consumption continues</cite>. Bullish for revenue but increases risk of demand destruction.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex reaches $725B in 2026, up 77% YoY; 75% allocated to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="27-1">Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, Microsoft $120B</cite>; <cite index="24-6,24-7">$600B annual revenue gap between hyperscaler AI spending and AI ecosystem sales; gap widening in 2026 as capex accelerated faster than revenue projections</cite>. Sustains memory demand but ROI scrutiny rising.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; capacity 120-140K wafers/month
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="29-6,29-7">TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity could reach 120,000-140,000 wafers in 2026; including 50,000-60,000 wafers of new capacity from OSAT partners, total could approach 200,000 wafers/month</cite>. Eases backend bottleneck for HBM-equipped AI accelerators.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix maintains 57% HBM market share in Q4 2025; Samsung at 22%, Micron 21%
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="9-3,9-4">SK Hynix controlled 57% global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025; reported five-fold jump in quarterly profit in April and said HBM demand expected to exceed supply over next three years</cite>. Reinforces Hynix's structural lead.

news_pulse.headline: Top three memory makers have allocated full HBM output for 2026; Micron guides 68% gross margin in Q2
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="8-3,8-7">Top three memory makers allocated full HBM output for the year; every wafer allocated to HBM stack for Nvidia GPU denied to LPDDR5X module or consumer laptop SSD</cite>. Zero-sum game pressures consumer/enterprise pricing.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix announce $518B national semiconductor ecosystem project; new fabs in southwest Korea
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="40-1,40-2">Samsung and SK Hynix will each build two new semiconductor fabrication plants in South Korea's southwest as part of 800 trillion won ($518B) project</cite>. <cite index="42-3">Samsung's P5 facility operational by 2028, SK Hynix M15X by mid-2027</cite>. Long lead times delay supply relief.

news_pulse.headline: Memory cyclicality debate intensifies; Deutsche Bank flags TurboQuant and structural demand shift risk
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="6-9,6-10">Deutsche Bank wrote investors should continue to brace for continuous AI-related disruption as evidenced by TurboQuant; remains to be seen whether technique will create structural shift in demand</cite>. Bear case: algorithmic efficiency reduces memory intensity.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="43-2,43-3">SK hynix ADRs closed +13.75% overnight at $171.94; top 1% traders at Mirae Asset net-bought Samsung Electronics while net-selling SK hynix on July 22</cite>. Suggests sophisticated money taking profits on SK Hynix momentum into Seoul open while rotating into Samsung on relative valuation/catch-up trade. <cite index="41-1">Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.21%</cite>, creating gap-up risk for Korean names. Watch for intraday mean reversion if U.S. futures fade. No KOSPI options data in payload, but elevated volatility likely given 5%+ moves. ADR-KRX arbitrage tight overnight; expect flow convergence.
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI close and Samsung/SK Hynix settlement prices vs. ADR premiums; watch for profit-taking after 5-6% gap-up
Any Nvidia commentary on HBM3E supplier qualification or pricing negotiations (Samsung certification watch)
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates for DDR5/LPDDR5X/NAND (Q3 guidance confirmation)
Hyperscaler earnings commentary (AWS, Azure, GCP) on AI capex trajectory vs. $725B consensus
TSMC packaging capacity or CoWoS allocation announcements (watch for OSAT spillover to Amkor/ASE)
